audit_findings.title: Current debt interest burden is absent from historical owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $639.733 million increase in total debt from FY2025 to June 2026; normalized OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity-level OE forecast retains interest expense, but the $337.5 million anchor predates most of the additional borrowing and therefore does not contain its full recurring interest and tax effects.
audit_findings.evidence: As of September 30, 2025, our total debt was $702,202, including $390,000 in unsecured notes denominated in U.S. dollars issued in private placements and $187,613 of unsecured notes denominated in Euros issued in private placements.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated capital-structure mismatch, although the precise valuation error remains unresolved. Total debt rose from $702.202 million to $1,341.935 million. June-quarter interest expense was already $3.593 million above the prior-year quarter, but much of the new financing was raised only on May 28, 2026, so the reported period does not show a full-year burden. A recurring charge on $639.733 million of incremental debt is reasonably capable of materially reducing capitalized OE.
audit_findings.action: Build a June 2026 debt-by-instrument schedule, calculate a full-year interest run rate including the $250 million term loan, $592.426 million revolver balance, swaps, fees and taxes, then rerun all scenarios with normalized equity OE.

audit_findings.title: The JV may be valued both through earnings and the stakes bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $25.666 million, or approximately $0.42 per share and 0.49% of $5.286 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method JV earnings enter net earnings and OE, while the JV investment carrying amount appears to be added again through the stakes bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Woodward is accounting for its 50 % ownership interest in the JV using the equity method of accounting.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 2026 stakes bridge can be reconstructed almost exactly from $43.526 million of deferred-compensation securities plus the $25.666 million JV investment, totaling $69.192 million. The filing also reports $45.697 million of nine-month JV earnings. Whether those earnings were purged from OE remains unresolved, but even complete removal of the separately added JV carrying value would reduce base value by only about 0.49%, which is not enough to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $69.2 million stakes line and the OE ledger; if JV earnings remain in OE, remove the $25.666 million JV investment from the bridge and update per-share values.

audit_findings.title: Customer-funded material rights can create cashless earnings and non-excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $428.722 million of June 2026 material-right contract liabilities versus $474.851 million of cash; actual valuation adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Material-right releases can enter OE as revenue without current-period cash receipts, while customer funding still needed to satisfy associated obligations may be included in the bridge as surplus cash.
audit_findings.evidence: Remaining performance obligations related to material rights that have not yet been recognized in revenue as of September 30, 2025 was $ 513,570 , of which $ 13,517 is expected to be recognized in fiscal year 2026 , and the balance is expected to be recognized thereafter.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate a large exposure but not a completed valuation error. June 2026 material-right liabilities were $235.880 million from the JV formation and $192.842 million from engineering and development funding, together equal to about 90% of reported cash. Corresponding costs are recognized as the programs progress, so neither the entire liability nor the entire cash balance can automatically be treated as unavailable. Nevertheless, the scale is reasonably capable of materially changing both normalized OE and the cash bridge.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each year's material-right revenue with associated cost-to-fulfill amortization, roll forward the related contract assets and liabilities through June 2026, trace the original customer funding into cash uses, and rerun the bridge using only demonstrably surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: Deferred-compensation assets may have matching claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $43.526 million, or approximately $0.71 per share and 0.82% of $5.286 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Deferred-compensation securities are included in the stakes bridge even though cash-settled deferred-compensation obligations are liabilities senior to common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: Deferred compensation obligations that will be settled in cash are accounted for on an accrual basis in accordance with the terms of the underlying contract and are reflected in the Consolidated Balance Sheet as “Other liabilities.”
audit_findings.explanation: The $69.2 million stakes line appears to include the filed $43.526 million deferred-compensation investment balance. The filing confirms that related cash-settled obligations are recorded in other liabilities but does not disclose their amount. Even if the full securities balance were unavailable to shareholders, the maximum identified bridge reduction is about 0.82% of base equity value, insufficient to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 deferred-compensation liability subledger, match it against the $43.526 million securities balance, and net the matched obligation from the stakes bridge.

audit_findings.title: Known FY2025 one-offs are not visibly reconciled from OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $20.524 million pretax product-rationalization gain, $13.392 million tax benefit, and recurring business-development costs of $7.310 million in FY2025 and $5.902 million in FY2024; anchor effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Unremoved gains or incorrectly removed recurring costs increase FY2025 OE and can raise the fitted log-trend anchor used in every scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in other income in fiscal year 2025 compared to fiscal year 2024 was primarily attributable to a one-time gain related to product rationalization activities that was recognized in the current fiscal year that did not occur in the prior fiscal year.
audit_findings.explanation: The one-offs are demonstrated by the filing, but their retention in the OE series is not demonstrated because the adjustment ledger was not supplied. The two favorable FY2025 items are together roughly 10% of the $337.5 million anchor before allowing for their different tax bases, and the trend is already identified as endpoint-sensitive. Accordingly, erroneous treatment is reasonably capable of materially affecting the operating-value estimate.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the year-by-year OE ledger, verify removal of the $20.524 million gain and $13.392 million tax benefit, confirm that recurring business-development costs remained charged, recompute the log trend, and rerun all scenarios if any treatment was incorrect.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may not equal distributable common-equity value
audit_findings.magnitude: $474.851 million gross June 2026 cash balance; operating-cash, restriction and tax leakage unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds gross cash dollar for dollar even though operating requirements, foreign-location constraints and repatriation taxes could make part of it unavailable to common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: If these funds were needed to fund our operations or satisfy obligations in the United States, then they could be repatriated, and their repatriation into the United States may cause us to incur additional U.S. income taxes or foreign withholding taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: FY2025 filings show that $324.617 million of $327.431 million cash was held by foreign locations, but they also state that no significant repatriation restrictions were then known and that potential taxes could not be determined. No June 2026 jurisdictional schedule or minimum operating-cash requirement is supplied. The issue may reduce bridge value, but the record cannot establish the amount or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain June 2026 cash by entity and jurisdiction, identify trapped or operationally required balances, calculate unavoidable withholding and incremental income taxes net of credits, and rerun the bridge with the resulting distributable cash amount.
